idiom_name: Razor tag helper (ITagHelper) and IHtmlHelper extension methods; view components for larger fragments
implementation_notes: ASP.NET Core ships two documented helper mechanisms and keeps them deliberately parallel: tag helpers attach server-side code to HTML elements (registered per view or once in _ViewImports.cshtml with @addTagHelper) and HTML helpers are extension methods on IHtmlHelper invoked from Razor as @Html.*. The classic J2EE helper class corresponds to a tag helper class whose Process/ProcessAsync method writes the element and whose properties bind to attributes; a helper that renders a larger region with its own data becomes a view component or partial view instead. Prefer tag helpers in markup-shaped views because designers can read them, and HTML helpers for single-value formatting; both keep C# out of the .cshtml markup. A hierarchy of helper classes is justified only when several helpers share substantial derivation logic; otherwise one small tag helper per concern is the unit.
pitfalls: Tag helpers are not supported inside Razor components, and they only run on elements in scope (@addTagHelper or @tagHelperPrefix), so an unregistered helper renders as plain HTML without any error.
A tag helper that was not designed as self-closing silently suppresses its output when written as a self-closing tag.
Returning HtmlString or calling SetHtmlContent bypasses Razor's encoding - reserve it for markup you built yourself, never for user data.
Attribute names bind case-insensitively to properties; a renamed property stops matching and the helper quietly renders defaults at runtime.
